title: Leadership priority lens and decision matrix
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight playbook for the executive and leadership cohort to: 1) evaluate competing requests through a shared priority lens, 2) produce a concise decision matrix for resource allocation, and 3) feed a clean set of asks/announcements into the All-Hands and Exec Update cadence.

Context / why this now:
- We’ve moved from heavy quarterly planning to a faster three-week priority cycle; that speed requires a clearer decision surface.
- Several big asks are overlapping (Dedicated capacity roadmap, Private compliance sprint, hosted cost-optimization). We need a single view so engineering, product, and GTM are aligned.
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive: small set of criteria + a matrix + a short comms play for All-Hands.

Quick note about usage:
- Leadership uses the matrix during the weekly Priority Triage meeting (Mon 10–11a).
- Owners fill in the short two-column request template (brief ask + impact/metric) 24 hours before the meeting.
- Decisions are logged in the decision registry (see linked artifact CONFL-2026-PRIORITY-LENS).

Decision lens (ranked):
1) Customer continuity & revenue impact (blocking customers, imminent renewals)
2) Security & compliance risk (audit windows, legal/regulatory deadlines)
3) Time-to-revenue for new offerings (clear path to measurable ARR within 3–6 months)
4) Long-term platform health (latency/SLO, major reliability risks)
5) Leverage & multiplicative enablement (work that unlocks >1 team cheaply)
6) Strategic learning (modeling/ops research that materially improves unit costs)

How to score (simple):
- Each request gets a 0–3 score on tiers above (3 = very high / urgent, 0 = no impact).
- Add a bias penalty for scope creep: -1 if ask lacks a clear owner or rollout plan.
- Total score drives priority buckets: 12–18 = Do Now; 7–11 = Schedule/Timebox; 0–6 = Defer / Backlog.

Request template (one-pager, two columns):
- Column A (brief): Title, owner, 1-sentence ask, what success looks like (metric + timeframe), required headcount/infra, estimated cost this quarter.
- Column B (matrix inputs): Scores for the 6 lens items above, blockers, dependencies, rollback plan, comms impact (all-hands / press / enterprise).

Example (mock):
- Title: Private VPC onboarding for FinanceCorp (pilot)
- Owner: Tomás Ortega
- Ask: Reserve a private deployment slot and two-node on-prem appliance for integration testing; 8-week pilot support.
- Success: Pilot completes, FinanceCorp signs PO for Dedicated by end of Q2; revenue $360k ARR.
- Resource ask: 0.5 SWEs, 0.3 SRE, 1 Solutions SE for 8 weeks; estimated infra incremental spend $9k.
- Matrix scores: Customer impact 3, Security 3, TtR 2, Platform health 1, Leverage 1, Strategic learning 0 = total 10 -> Schedule/Timebox

All-Hands / Exec Update playbook (short):
- Goal: make 1–3 clear signals and 2 asks that employees can act on. Avoid long lists.
- Structure: 90s company headline, 2 wins (quantified), 1 risk/ask, 30s call-to-action + where to comment.
- Example signals to surface: Dedicated capacity SLA improvements (metrics), simplified pricing experiment for embeddings, upcoming private-deployment pilot partners.
- Ask template for the company: "We need 50 volunteers across Eng, SRE, and Solutions to help run pilot readiness checklists next month" -> include sign-up link + owner + time commitment.

Execution calendar (next 8 weeks):
- Week A (Mar 1–7): Finalize priority lens in Exec; circulate small training doc for request owners.
- Week B (Mar 8–14): Triage meeting: collect first batch of requests; populate matrix; pre-announce top 2 items for All-Hands.
- Week C (Mar 15–21): All-Hands: run the 90s headline + 2 wins + 1 ask. Publish decision registry update same day.
- Weeks D–F: Owners execute; weekly syncs with ops for tracking; mid-point check (end of Week F) to evaluate metrics.

Metrics to track per request (minimum):
- Owner-provided success metric (primary), weekly progress % to goal, engineering effort logged (swe-weeks), infra spend vs estimate, customer feedback (NPS or CSAT for pilots), rollback triggers (yes/no).

Common friction patterns (notes to leadership):
- Requests without a hard customer/metric anchor drift. Insist on an objective measure or score them lower.
- Too many "pilot" asks without conversion thresholds — require ROI assumptions up front.
- Cross-team dependencies without a single integrator cause stalls; require integration owner in Column B.

Unresolved questions / open choices:
- Do we require a minimum score for Executive sponsorship? (proposal: score >= 14 needed for Exec sponsor)
- How to treat early-stage R&D that scores low on immediate impact but is strategic for 12–18 months? (proposal: create a separate "strategic runway" bucket with time-limited funding)
- Should recruiting commitments be considered a hard resource reservation or budgeted separately in headcount planning?

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Decision paralysis with too many medium-priority items. Mitigation: cap Do Now to 3 items per cycle and enforce schedule for remainder.
- Risk: Invisible work (maintenance) starves new initiatives. Mitigation: require a health baseline for platform SLOs every cycle; if SLO drift > 5% prioritize platform work.

Communication templates (short snippets):
- All-Hands call-to-action: "We’re prioritizing X, Y, Z this cycle. If you’re working on a project that would be deprioritized, post a 2-line note in #priority-triage or file JIRA-4201 by Wednesday."
- Exec-update headline: "Decided: Pilot A (Do Now), Scale B (Schedule), Defer C. See decision register."

Next steps (owners):
- Aisha: finalize the scoring rubric doc and short owner training (by Mar 5).
- Ben: wire up the decision registry view in Confluence and add the request template (by Mar 9).
- Sophie: draft the All-Hands 90s headline and volunteer sign-up flow (by Mar 12).
- Tomás: prepare the first pilot request with full Column A/B populated (by Mar 8).

Appendix: quick rubric cheatsheet (for request owners)
- Customer impact: 3 if revenue at risk / deals blocked; 2 if strong customer ask with clear ROI; 1 informal interest; 0 none.
- Security: 3 if regulatory/legal deadline; 2 if security bug with elevated risk; 1 if internal control improvement; 0 none.
- TtR: 3 if can convert to revenue under 6 weeks; 2 if 1–3 months; 1 if 3–6 months; 0 otherwise.
- Platform health: 3 if SLO/orch degradation > 20%; 2 if >10%; 1 if minor; 0 normal.
- Leverage: 3 unlocks multiple teams / products; 2 unlocks one other team; 1 minimal; 0 none.
- Strategic learning: 3 moves needle on unit economics or model quality; 2 useful signal; 1 speculative; 0 no.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the matrix accessible — people will game shiny scores. Emphasize documentation over gaming.
- This doc should live with the decision registry and be linked into the All-Hands prep folder.
- We'll iterate the rubric after two cycles and publish examples of accepted/rejected requests to reduce friction.

-- end of draft --
